title: Review: Apple's M6 iMac is pricey, but it's still a good choice for a clean desk
gist: Apple's M6 iMac is a box-ticking internal refresh that raises the entry price to $1,499 ($200 more than the M4 launch) while keeping 256GB base storage; its M6 runs in an ~18 W envelope, making it 5–12% slower than M6 Mac mini/MacBook Pro but 15–40% faster than the M4 iMac. Ars says M1 owners needn't upgrade and a refurbished M4 is the best value.

insights.claim: The M6 iMac starts at $1,499, $200 more than the $1,299 starting price held by every entry-level iMac from the 2019 Intel model through the M4.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple is pushing desktop ASPs higher, a margin lever amid component cost pressures.

insights.claim: The $899 Mac mini is $800 cheaper than the iMac with the same chip, RAM and storage, meaning buyers pay a large premium for the iMac's design and integration.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Highlights Apple's design premium pricing power.
insights.locator: I still really like the effect

insights.claim: Base $1,499 iMac uses a cut-down M6 with 10 CPU and 10 GPU cores, max 24GB RAM, 256GB starting storage, two Thunderbolt ports, and requires an $80 keyboard upsell for Touch ID; the $1,699 model gets the full chip, four ports and 32GB/2TB options.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple's upsell ladder steers buyers to higher-margin configurations.

insights.claim: Apple Silicon iMacs have never received a base storage upgrade beyond 256GB.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Storage upsells remain a profit lever Apple is unwilling to give up.
insights.locator: The iMac’s evolution has been slow

insights.claim: The reviewer argues owners of any Apple Silicon iMac who are satisfied with performance and don't need more RAM or displays gain nothing worth upgrading for, since the M1 remains perfectly serviceable six years on.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Long Mac replacement cycles temper hardware refresh-driven revenue.
insights.locator: If you have any kind of Apple Silicon iMac

insights.claim: The reviewer says a refurbished or discounted M4 iMac offers the best value, and the biggest dividing line in Apple Silicon iMac history is between the M3 and M4 models, not M4 and M6.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Two-generation silicon jumps no longer guarantee compelling upgrades.
insights.quote: But the brightest dividing line in the Apple Silicon iMac model history is between the M3 and M4 model, not the M4 and M6 model.
insights.locator: The M6 iMac builds on that

insights.claim: The M6 iMac is described as a box-ticking upgrade that keeps the internals current without changing who the iMac is for or its place in Apple's lineup.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: The iMac is a maintenance product line, not a growth driver.
insights.quote: It’s a box-ticking upgrade, and the box being ticked is “keep the insides up to date.”

insights.claim: The Apple M6 has 12 CPU cores (2 super, 4 performance, 6 efficiency), up to 12 GPU cores, a doubled 32-core Neural Engine, and GPU neural accelerators carried over from the M5 that speed local AI workloads such as MetalFX upscaling and frame generation.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple is embedding more on-device AI compute across its Mac line.
insights.locator: A quick recap on the M6

insights.claim: The iMac's M6 averages about 18 W under sustained load versus roughly 28 W in the Mac mini and 14-inch MacBook Pro, making those machines 5 to 8 percent faster in multi-core CPU and 8 to 12 percent faster in graphics.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Thermal design, not chip, sets real-world performance differentiation across Apple's lineup.
insights.locator: The iMac is slower than either

insights.claim: Versus the M4 iMac, the M6 iMac is 15 to 20 percent faster single-core, 20 to 30 percent faster multi-core, and 20 to 40 percent faster in graphics, with Blender GPU tests benefiting further from neural accelerators.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Quantifies generational gains for Apple Silicon.
insights.locator: That still makes it a solid upgrade

insights.claim: The 16GB M6 offers 153 GB/s of memory bandwidth versus 170 GB/s for 24GB and 32GB versions, a minor performance difference.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Memory configuration affects bandwidth-sensitive workloads modestly.
insights.locator: The M6 in the Mac mini

insights.claim: The reviewer says Apple's Mac Studio has effectively made Apple admit it doesn't want to make the Mac Pro anymore, while the iMac remains a backward-looking design aimed at simple office and kiosk users.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Signals Apple's pro desktop consolidation around Mac Studio.
